analysis.investment_thesis: JK Paper passes a few Graham screens — D/E of 0.37, P/B of 1.16, and a near-Graham-Number price (~INR 392 vs. current INR 375) — but its trailing P/E of 25.4x far exceeds my 15x ceiling, and earnings have collapsed 66% from INR 1,208 Cr (2023) to INR 412 Cr (2025), destroying any confidence in normalised earning power. A commodity-paper business with paper-thin 4.55% operating margins offers no margin of safety for the disciplined investor.
key_strengths: Conservative balance sheet: D/E of 0.37 and total debt declining from INR 3,137 Cr (2022) to INR 1,885 Cr (2025)
Long earnings history: profitable every year in the 9-year dataset with 24.8% net profit CAGR, demonstrating a going-concern track record Graham respects
P/B of 1.16 and Graham Number ~INR 392 means price is near — though not yet firmly below — intrinsic book-based value
key_risks: Savage earnings cyclicality: net profit swung from INR 1,208 Cr (2023) to INR 412 Cr (2025) — a 66% collapse in two years; Graham demands stable earning power, not a roller-coaster
Commodity business with no moat: paper is undifferentiated, margins are structurally thin (4.55% operating margin in 2025), and pricing power is zero against global pulp costs
Trailing P/E of 25.4x exceeds my hard 15x ceiling; forward P/E of 7.64 relies on analyst projections I refuse to capitalise — Mr. Market's optimism is not a fact
red_flags: Operating income crashed from INR 2,012 Cr (2023) to INR 928 Cr (2025) — more than halved — with no structural explanation, signalling commodity-cycle exposure
Free cash flow plunged from INR 1,552 Cr (2023) to INR 365 Cr (2025), eroding the one year that looked genuinely attractive
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Applying my quantitative filters, JK Paper is a mixed picture. The balance sheet is respectable: D/E of 0.37 is well inside my 0.5 ceiling, borrowings have fallen four consecutive years, and operating cash flow has been positive for all five years shown. P/B of 1.16 is in acceptable — if not ideal — territory, and my Graham Number calculation (√(22.5 × ~22.7 EPS × ~301 BVPS) ≈ INR 392) puts the current price of INR 375 marginally below that threshold. These are the facts that keep me from recommending outright avoidance.

However, the earning-power requirement — the cornerstone of my method — is decisively undermined by cyclicality. Net profit has swung between INR 237 Cr and INR 1,208 Cr over five years; I cannot construct a reliable "normalised" EPS. On trailing earnings the P/E is 25.4x, more than 70% above my ceiling. Paper is a commodity with no pricing power, low barriers to entry, and operating margins that compressed to a mere 4.55% in 2025. I do not pay 25x for thin, volatile earnings regardless of what analysts project for next year — Mr. Market's forward estimates have a poor track record in cyclical industries. Existing holders may sit tight as the Forward P/E of 7.64 could reward patience if the cycle turns, but there is insufficient margin of safety for fresh capital.
